questions.question: Define mitigation and explain why it is considered the cornerstone of disaster management. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Definemitigationandexplainwhyitisconsideredthecornerstoneofdisaster
  • management.
  • Mitigation refers to long-term measures taken to reduce or eliminate the risk and
  • impact of disasters before they occur.
  • • It focuses on risk reduction rather than response after a disaster.
  • • Includes structural measures such as earthquake-resistant buildings, flood control
  • dams and cyclone shelters.
  • • Includes non-structural measures like policies, land-use planning and building
  • regulations.
  • • Reduces loss of life, property damage and economic loss.
  • • Strengthens community resilience and preparedness.
  • • Therefore it is considered the cornerstone of disaster management.

questions.question: Explain why a rescuer should allow for complete "chest recoil" after each compression and why a firm surface is necessary for infants. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explainwhyarescuershouldallowforcomplete"chestrecoil"aftereach
  • compression and why a firm surface is necessary for infants.

questions.question: Discuss how a fire extinguisher works to stop a fire. / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Discusshowafireextinguisherworkstostopafire.
  • Fire extinguishers are designed to control small fires by interrupting the process
  • of combustion. They work by removing one or more elements of the fire triangle.
  • • Cooling: Water extinguishers lower the temperature below the ignition point.
  • • Smothering: Foam or CO₂ removes oxygen from the fire.
  • • Chemical interruption: Dry powder stops the chemical chain reaction of fire.
  • • Prevents the spread of fire.
  • • Provides time for safe evacuation and fire control.
questions.source_exam: MGU-UGP (HONOURS) 2024 Admission Regular Exam Sem 4, March 2026

questions.question: Write an essay on first aid measures for poisoning and drowning. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Writeanessayonfirstaidmeasuresforpoisoninganddrowning.
  • Poisoning and drowning are common emergencies that require immediate first aid.
  • Quick and correct action can save lives before professional medical help arrives.
  • First Aid for Poisoning
  • Poisoning occurs when harmful substances enter the body through ingestion,
  • inhalation, injection or skin contact.
  • • Identify the type of poison if possible
  • • Call emergency medical services immediately
  • • Remove the victim from the source of poison
  • • Keep the person calm and comfortable
  • • Move the victim to fresh air if poison is inhaled
  • • Do not induce vomiting unless instructed by medical professionals
  • • Wash the skin with clean water if poison contacts skin
  • • Keep the poison container or sample for doctors
  • First Aid for Drowning
  • Drowning occurs when breathing is impaired because water enters the airway.
  • • Remove the victim from water as quickly and safely as possible
  • • Check breathing and pulse
  • • Start CPR immediately if the person is not breathing
  • • Loosen tight clothing and keep the victim warm
  • • Place in recovery position if breathing resumes
  • • Seek immediate medical assistance
  • • Monitor the victim until professional help arrives

questions.question: Differentiate between Intentional and Unintentional fire. Give examples. / [CO3] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• DifferentiatebetweenIntentionalandUnintentionalfire.Giveexamples.
  • Fires can be broadly classified into intentional and unintentional fires depending on
  • how they are caused. Understanding this difference helps in prevention and
  • investigation.
  • Intentional Fire
  • Intentional fire is deliberately started by a person with a specific purpose.
  • Examples include
  • • Arson for insurance fraud
  • • Riots and vandalism
  • • Terrorist attacks
  • • Revenge or sabotage
  • These fires are usually planned and may involve accelerants, causing serious damage
  • to life and property.
  • Unintentional Fire
  • Unintentional fire occurs accidentally due to negligence or technical faults.
  • Examples include
  • • Electrical short circuits
  • • Gas leaks and explosions
  • • Unattended cooking
  • • Improper handling of flammable substances
  • • Faulty electrical appliances
  • Such fires are not deliberate and often result from human error or equipment
  • failure.
